title: Singleton coefficient of the minority indicator
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $i$ be a coordinate. The Fourier coefficient of its minority indicator at $\{i\}$ is $-\widehat f(\{i\})/2$ if the mean of the real-valued form of $f$ is nonnegative, and is $\widehat f(\{i\})/2$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $i$ be
a coordinate. The Fourier coefficient of its minority indicator at $\{i\}$ is $-\widehat
f(\{i\})/2$ when the mean of $f$ is nonnegative, and $\widehat f(\{i\})/2$ when the mean
is negative.
